content.summary: The least used resource pools are Planning scanners, Intake clerks and Dispatch clerks among those with the lowest utilization figures. Intake clerks are at 5.2% utilization, the lowest of the pools with a stated utilization, and Dispatch clerks are at 8.8%. Planning scanners are at 21.6% and their idle unit time is 229 hours.
keyChanges: Intake clerks (employee) utilization is 5.2% with idle unit time of 184 hours.
Dispatch clerks (employee) utilization is 8.8% with idle unit time of 178 hours.
Planning scanners (machine) utilization is 21.6% with idle unit time of 229 hours.
risks: Low utilization of these pools does not mean they can be cut, since they still carry cost, for example Planners cost INR 75,886 and Intake clerks cost INR 21,404.
content.bottleneckExplanation: Polishing is the bottleneck, with its Polishing wheels pool at 89.6% utilization, so the low-use pools are not the constraint.

recommendations.title: Review staffing of Intake clerks and Dispatch clerks
recommendations.rationale: Both pools show very low utilization, so their hours could be checked against actual workload before any change is considered.

recommendations.title: Test any capacity change in Scenario Lab
recommendations.rationale: Any reduction of an underused pool has not been simulated; create a scenario in Scenario Lab, run it and compare it with this run.

assumptions: Utilization is taken as the share of the run's working time each pool was busy, as stated in the simulation.
limitations: The evidence gives utilization for each pool but does not say what cutting any pool would do to output or delivery.
Lowest utilization is judged only from the figures shown; the evidence does not rank every pool.
